yeneen:study:1.title: Yeneen houssayi gen. et sp. nov. and an overview of the sauropod titanosaurian diversity from Cerro Overo – La Invernada area (Bajo de la Carpa Formation, Santonian), North Patagonia, Argentina (Historical Biology, 2026)

facts.statement: Yeneen is a titanosaur sauropod dinosaur genus.
Yeneen lived during the Late Cretaceous Santonian age.
The type locality of Yeneen is the Bajo de la Carpa Formation in Argentina.
facts.quote: Type locality: Bajo de la Carpa Formation

facts.statement: The genus Yeneen contains the single species Yeneen houssayi.
Yeneen is known from at least one partial skeleton.
facts.quote: known from at least one partial skeleton

facts.statement: A third specimen, MAU-Pv-LI-731, contains disarticulated axial and appendicular bones and has not yet been referred to Yeneen houssayi.
facts.quote: MAU-Pv-LI-731, includes disarticulated axial and appendicular bones and is still undergoing preparation

facts.statement: The generic name Yeneen comes from a Tehuelche word referring to cold and winter weather.
facts.quote: The generic name, Yeneen, is the name of an entity in Tehuelche (Aonikenk) culture tied to the cold and winter weather

facts.statement: The specific epithet houssayi honors Nobel laureate Bernardo Alberto Houssay.
facts.quote: The specific name, houssayi, honors Bernardo Alberto Houssay, a recipient of the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Yeneen within Saltasauroidea, in a subgroup referred to as "Clade A", diverging after Narambuenatitan and before Overosaurus.
facts.quote: placed Yeneen as part of the clade Saltasauroidea, in a more exclusive group the researchers referred to as "Clade A", where it diverges after Narambuenatitan but before Overosaurus

facts.statement: Yeneen lived in a semi‑arid fluvial and aeolian paleoenvironment.
facts.quote: Its sediments represent fluvial and aeolian systems, with a semi-arid paleoenvironment

facts.statement: Other titanosaurs from the same formation include Bonitasaura, Inawentu, Overosaurus, Rinconsaurus, and Traukutitan.
facts.quote: Sauropods include the diverse fellow titanosaurs Bonitasaura, Inawentu, Overosaurus, Rinconsaurus, and Traukutitan

facts.statement: Yeneen is dated to the Santonian stage, approximately 85.7 to 83.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Santonian (85.7 to 83.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database records a single fossil occurrence of Yeneen.

rejected.statement: Yeneen was described as a new genus and species by Filippi et al. in 2026.
